subject: SIG: dependency disclosure & evidence request — Redwood Inference
messages:
From: Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@acmepayments.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Security Intake <security@acmepayments.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG: Request for dependency disclosure & evidence — Redwood Inference

Ben / Redwood team,

As part of our SIG review for an upcoming integration with your hosted inference API, Acme Payments needs a consolidated dependency disclosure and supporting evidence. Specifically we are looking for: 
- A roster of subprocessors (cloud providers, telemetry/observability, support/CS tools, identity providers, vendor-managed services) with: purpose, data categories processed, country of processing, and contractual data access level.
- Relevant evidence artifacts: SOC 2 report (if available), dataflow/network diagram showing telemetry egress, and copies of third-party processor agreements or attestations where available.
- For telemetry: list of endpoints (e.g. Datadog/Prometheus/Sentry), what data is sent (metrics, traces, logs, payload snippets), and retention windows.

We attached our auditor intake form for format preferences. Could you confirm whether this is something you can provide and your expected timeline? We ideally need a preliminary roster by end of week (Fri, 25 Jun) and evidence bundle shortly after.

Two clarifying questions from our side: (1) Do you consider cloud IaaS (AWS/GCP) and marketplace partners as subprocessors on your register? (2) Do you have a single point of contact for vendor questions?

Thanks,
Megan Ortiz
Senior Security Program Manager
Acme Payments

---
Attachment: auditor-intake-form.pdf (1 page)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>

Megan — thanks for the clear ask. We can handle this. 

Quick answers to your clarifying Qs: we enumerate IaaS providers (AWS/GCP), telemetry vendors, and managed service vendors on our subprocessor register — yes, they are included when they process customer data or telemetry tied to customer workloads. We maintain a single intake point for third-party questions; I've looped in Rishi (Security) and Laura (Legal) who will own the evidence pack.

Proposed timeline: 
- Wed, 23 Jun: Preliminary subprocessor roster (CSV) with high-level fields.
- Fri, 25 Jun: Evidence bundle (SOC 2 + network flow diagram + sample contracts/attestations).
If that works for you we'll prioritize. If you need earlier delivery on any specific vendor, tell us which one and we'll escalate.

I will attach our working mapping file once Rishi populates the roster.

Ben Carter
Head of Revenue 
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Megan Ortiz <megan.ortiz@acmepayments.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 08:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG: Request for dependency disclosure & evidence — Redwood Inference

Megan / Ben — I pulled together an initial roster and a short note on telemetry/dataflow. See summary below and attached CSV + diagram. We will expand fields and include contacts/contracts in the full bundle.

Summary (initial):
- Cloud Providers:
  - AWS (us-west-2): compute, object storage, KMS; processes customer request payloads and logs.
  - GCP (us-east1): backup and analytics workloads (limited customer-identifying data).
- Telemetry/Observability:
  - Datadog (metrics + APM traces): agent-forwarded metrics and traces from runtime; no customer PII is intentionally captured — we mask prompt text at capture points. Retention: metrics 90 days, traces 30 days.
  - Sentry (error aggregation): stack traces and error context; default sampling excludes large payloads; retention 30 days.
- Support / Customer Success Tools:
  - Zendesk: support tickets and user-provided logs (ticket-level attachments may contain customer data).
  - Intercom: product usage events and messaging; used for onboarding flows.
- Identity / Access:
  - Okta: identity provider for Redwood employees; not a customer-facing authentication for hosted API.

Dataflow notes: our runtime applies prefix/KV caching and token redaction before exporting telemetry. Network diagram (attached) highlights telemetry egress to Datadog and Sentry via TLS, and cohort-level metrics exported to a GCP analytics project.

Attachments: subproc_roster_v1.csv, network_flow_diagram_v1.pdf

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

---
Attachment: subproc_roster_v1.csv (partial export)
Attachment: network_flow_diagram_v1.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)

Thanks Rishi — that is helpful. A couple of follow-ups to make the SIG intake smoother on our side: 
1) Can you provide a contract reference or point of contact for each vendor (legal or vendor manager email) so our procurement team can request any missing attestations?
2) For telemetry: can you confirm whether any raw prompt text (or identifiable customer input) is ever sent to Datadog/Sentry in full, even transiently? If so, how is it redacted?
3) Are there any on-prem or self-hosted deployments where telemetry is routed differently (we have a few customers requiring that telemetry never leaves their VPC)?

We also attached our SIG parent questionnaire link below — if you prefer we can accept the answers in the spreadsheet format you sent.

If you can give those items by Thu EOD (24 Jun) we'll proceed with the SIG intake on our side.

Megan Ortiz

- We uploaded a CSV with vendor contact columns and contract refs; procurement-sig-mapping.xlsx has the vendor point-of-contact column filled where available.
